roots.explanation: The scoped set difference is exactly agentLoop → zcodeLoop. Sorted-array positions amplify one implementation service substitution.
roots.effect: Agents uses the registered factory; shared services remain present. No missing agents/llm/tools service is implied.

roots.explanation: Stock registers the inbox fold and wire view; ZCode folds splices privately and does not register this projection.
roots.effect: Projection readers cannot request the standard inbox state/view, even when both final private queues are empty.
roots.owner: Existing sessionProjections.register / stateOf / wire view; extract or reproduce the loop-owned inbox definition without activating a second loop.

roots.explanation: ZCode adds its explicit CLI identity prefix before the same dsh system body. This rule accepts only that exact prefix.
roots.effect: The model receives a different product identity; retained dsh policy body is unchanged.

roots.explanation: Stock persists the admitted tool schemas in request/header; the event bridge writes only provider/model.
roots.effect: requestHeader reconstruction loses the tool snapshot; successful tool execution does not restore the durable request envelope.
roots.owner: Existing Session request/header / canonicalHeader / foldRequestHeader and ctx.tools.schemas; connect the admitted request tool set.

roots.explanation: The stock request/context event has no aligned ZCode event. This is a missing event, not index noise.
roots.effect: Session.requestContext() has no provider/model/context metadata to fold.
roots.owner: Existing prepared LLM call context and Session.requestContext; emit the installed request/context contract.

roots.explanation: ZCode writes a header for every model request and labels later ones change; stock uses header equality and series boundaries.
roots.effect: Redundant headers and a series → change reason alter durable request provenance.
roots.owner: Existing canonicalHeader/headerEquals and Session request-header folding; mirror stock admission/series rules.

roots.explanation: The ZCode runtime buffers tool input deltas before publishing model_streaming events. Consecutive argument fragments coalesce to exactly the same id/name/index/argument string.
roots.effect: Token arrival granularity changes; argument bytes, blocks and usage must remain equal. Unknown stream fields do not qualify.

roots.explanation: flushPendingAssistant commits on the first scheduled call and clears the pending assistant; the later call is logged separately but its content block never reaches that assistant surface.
roots.effect: A multi-tool assistant surface loses a tool-call block even though both tools execute. This is a missing surface block, not a scheduler-order allowance.
roots.owner: Existing dsh assistant/message ContentBlock array and tool-call journal; retain the complete model call set before surface commit.

roots.explanation: The bridge marks an incoming finish as consumed without adding its finish chunk, then suppresses its fallback.
roots.effect: Persisted assistant streams lose the terminal reason although text and usage remain. Replay/assembly defaults can conceal truncation or other finish semantics.
roots.owner: Existing AssistantStreamAccumulator and dsh finish chunks; preserve the received reason on the durable stream.

roots.explanation: update_goal completion defers a tool-goal notice; stock consumes it as next-step inbox and user/message. ZCode tools.execute maps only content/error back to the engine.
roots.effect: The closing instruction and its durable source are absent. The scripted fixture still returns a closing answer and therefore does not prove instruction delivery.
roots.owner: Existing dsh tools scheduler deferred context / stock acceptContext callback and next-step inbox; carry deferred context through the bridge. No new host plugin is evidenced.

roots.explanation: Matched events are compared independently of their array position. Only fields equal to their semantic peer, or separately classified peer fields, may collapse here.
roots.effect: Raw event order still differs: inbox claim precedes turn/start in ZCode; scheduled tool/call records may precede earlier results. This count is positional amplification, not a claim of equal execution timing.

roots.explanation: A seq/sourceEventSeqs/projection boundary value resolves to the same aligned event on each side.
roots.effect: Different event counts/order change numeric offsets without changing the referenced event.

roots.explanation: An assistant message paired by turn/step has a different normalized generated id after the missing notice changes identity collection order.
roots.effect: Only a generated assistant message id is treated as statistical noise; source identities/revisions and content are still checked.
